To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the performance of space time feature detectors is highly dependent on the type of actions and the complexity of the background, that the performance of local feature descriptors is highly dependent on their ability to capture the motion information, and that the combination of the best performing feature detector and descriptor yields the best recognition performance.

(1) local features are more effective than global features for action recognition, (2) the best results are obtained using regular sampling of local space time features, and (3) the best results for local space time features are obtained using the histogram of oriented gradients as the local feature descriptor

(a) space time features can be used for action recognition in realistic settings; (b) regular sampling of space-time features outperforms all other tested feature detectors; (c) the best feature descriptor is the HOG3D; (d) the best combination of features, detector and descriptor depends on the dataset.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of local space time features for human action recognition and provides a common experimental setup for the evaluation of existing methods.
the analysis of space time features and the evaluation of existing methods.
a systematic evaluation of existing space time feature extraction techniques for action recognition and we believe that it will be useful for future research in this direction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the best performing feature is the regular sampling of the space time volume, followed by the space time interest point detector proposed by Dollar and Zitnick.
the best results are obtained by combining a space time interest point detector, such as the Harris3D detector, and the HOG3D descriptor, which outperforms the other methods by a significant margin.
the choice of the feature detector is more important than that of the descriptor for action recognition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the best performing method for space time action recognition is a combination of regular sampling of space-time interest points and a dense sampling of local space time features.
the choice of a feature detector and descriptor is important for action recognition.
the best performing features for human action recognition in realistic settings are obtained using a regular sampling grid with the dense trajectories approach.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the performance of space time features is highly dependent on the dataset and that no single feature detector or descriptor is superior for all action datasets.
local features are a viable alternative to more sophisticated approaches for action recognition, especially in realistic settings where large amounts of training data is not available.
the choice of the feature descriptor is a crucial factor in action recognition and that there is no single best feature detector and descriptor combination.
